upper_bound.quote:
Indeed, since all primes are at least $2$,
\[
2^{|D|}\le w(D\setminus\{p\})<a_1
\]
for the corresponding $p$.
upper_bound.witness: Counterexample: take $a_1=2$. The greedy sequence consists exactly of the even integers, so $\mathcal C=\{\{2\}\}$. For the terminal member $D=\{2\}$ and $p=2$, one has $w(D\setminus\{p\})=w(\varnothing)=1<2=a_1$, but the asserted inequality is $2^{|D|}=2\le1$, which is false. Only $2^{|D|-1}\le w(D\setminus\{p\})$ follows.
upper_bound.load_bearing: This is the written bound on the cardinalities of terminal members. Without a valid bound, Lemma 1 cannot establish that there are finitely many terminal members, so the descent does not establish a finite prime universe containing every member of $\mathcal C$.

parsed.notes: Mapping: lower_bound is bounded-rank finiteness via the infinite sunflower argument; upper_bound is weight descent to bounded terminal supports and a finite prime universe. Reduction uses support self-duality and residue-class counting.
